closure.contract: Precommit each novel axiom geometry as a local admitted equality; instantiate and audit it in its own local terms; freeze it and each total question before comparison search; promote a raw candidate T only after preservation and reflection of equality, then carry an explicit (T, phi, pi) translational form through return, operation, orientation, curvature, quotient factorization, witnessed openness, and next-basis transfer.
required_order: internally audited and frozen frame equalities
GeomEquiv admission by preservation and reflection
return, extension, reversal, curvature, and operation naturality
quotient ResolvedIn or witnessed OpenIn with translation lineage

fixed_frame.contract: Check each frozen local algebra and every supplied cross-presentation map using ordinary group/isomorphism verification. This is a strong baseline: it may accept noncanonical isomorphisms and orientation reversal.
not_in_contract: constructing Pole x B occurrence fibres
choosing frame equality after seeing a comparison
treating lack of a unique isomorphism as failure

claim_boundary: Executed bounded comparative proxy; neither arm is an actual ASI or Aristotle run. The experiment compares verification architectures over identical frozen symbolic artifacts, not model capability.
comparative_hypothesis: An explicit origin-free ReferenceFrame/GeomEquiv pipeline produces auditable cross-presentation transport, obstruction, and frame-qualified resolution/openness certificates that per-artifact kernel acceptance plus standard isomorphism checking does not itself record.
falsification: The arms do not receive byte-identical frozen mathematical inputs.
A frame equality or total question is revised after a candidate comparison is inspected.
The fixed-frame baseline rejects a valid ordinary isomorphism merely because it is noncanonical or reverses orientation.
The closure arm classifies missing data or non-selection as OpenIn.
The closure arm emits OpenIn without x~y and Q(x)!=Q(y).
The closure arm must secretly privilege a canonical frame to produce its certificates.
On richer paired studies, the strong fixed-frame baseline recovers the same auditable relations with equal or lower cost.

frontier_scaleup_contract.allowed_tools: precommit the same model, proof kernels, retrieval tools, and resource limits for both verification arms
artifact_requirements: carrier and local operations or axioms
locally assumed admitted equality geometry and its internal coherence obligations
frontier_scaleup_contract.budget_rule: record equal model and tool access plus wall time, tokens, proof-check time, and evidence bytes
frontier_scaleup_contract.candidate_rule: candidate search begins only after both local axiom-geometry assumptions, their instantiated equality tables, and all total questions are frozen
frontier_scaleup_contract.geometry_rule: A novel geometry is evaluated under its own precommitted admitted equality. The evaluator may report an internal coherence counterexample but may not redefine that equality after seeing another frame or a candidate translator.

shared_input.candidate_visibility: Both arms receive the same raw post-freeze candidate maps. Neither receives the other arm's verdicts.
shared_input.source: Fresh deterministic executions of the two isolated D4 learners, followed by isolated instantiation and internal audit of each precommitted local axiom-geometry assumption before candidate construction.
shared_input.source_boundary: The bounded fixture supplies independently learned and frozen presentations; it is not frontier-agent evidence.

success_is_not: proof that ordinary mathematics cannot express isomorphism
proof that closure ASI is more capable
an Aristotle or open-ended ASI result
